slides.title: Double the radius. ==Eight times== the volume.

slides.stem: Sphere $A$ has a radius of $r$, and sphere $B$ has a radius of $2r$. The volume of sphere $B$ is how many times the volume of sphere $A$?

slides.intro: Volume multiplies length three times, so the factor triples up.
slides.trapWhy: $2$ treats volume like a single length. $4$ stops at area. Three dimensions, three doublings.

slides.title: Raise the scale factor to the dimension
slides.body:
Scale every length by $k$ and lengths grow by $k$, areas by $k^2$, volumes by $k^3$.

This works for any shape — spheres, cones, boxes — which is why the SAT can ask it without giving you a single formula.
